IVX AUTONOMOUS SELF-HEALING — FULL CODE SCAN, CRASH RECOVERY AND 24/7 STABILITY

PRIORITY: P0
MODE: CONTINUOUS EXECUTION
OBJECTIVE: Make IVX continuously inspect its complete software stack, detect failures immediately, contain crashes, diagnose root causes, produce safe repairs, validate them, and restore service with minimum owner intervention.

IMPORTANT REALITY STANDARD

Do not claim that crashes can never occur.

Required target:

- crash detection within seconds
- automatic containment or rollback within minutes
- root-cause diagnosis with evidence
- safe repair through branch, tests, CI, deployment and verification
- truthful status at every stage
- no production mutation without required approval

==================================================
PHASE 1 — CONTINUOUS END-TO-END CODE SCAN
==================================================

Continuously scan:

- backend
- Expo application
- Android native code
- iOS native code
- web and landing application
- GitHub Actions
- Render deployment configuration
- Supabase schema, migrations and RLS
- authentication
- IVX IA Chat
- autonomous workers
- API routes
- queues
- scheduled jobs
- media uploads
- reels
- notifications
- registration
- owner controls
- APK/AAB build configuration
- dependencies
- secrets exposure
- duplicate and dead code
- unreachable code
- broken imports
- TypeScript
- lint
- test coverage
- database queries
- memory leaks
- network timeouts
- retries
- race conditions
- duplicate subscriptions
- infinite loading states
- startup failures

Run scans in small isolated batches.

Do not modify hundreds of files in one task.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — REAL-TIME CRASH DETECTION
==================================================

Detect automatically:

- mobile crashes
- JavaScript exceptions
- native Android crashes
- native iOS crashes
- backend exceptions
- HTTP 500 errors
- repeated HTTP 401/403 errors
- database connection failures
- Render restart loops
- failed deployments
- GitHub Actions failures
- worker heartbeat loss
- stuck jobs
- message duplication
- blank screens
- infinite loading
- memory exhaustion
- API latency spikes
- upload failures
- authentication failures
- SHA mismatch

Create an incident immediately containing:

- incident ID
- trace ID
- severity
- affected platform
- affected route/module
- stack trace
- current GitHub SHA
- current production SHA
- first detected time
- last detected time
- occurrence count
- affected users
- suspected file/function
- current mitigation
- repair status

==================================================
PHASE 3 — IMMEDIATE CONTAINMENT
==================================================

When a critical crash is detected:

1. Stop additional unsafe deployments.
2. Mark the current release DEGRADED.
3. Preserve logs and evidence.
4. Check whether the previous release was healthy.
5. If the new deployment caused the incident:
   - trigger rollback
   - capture rollback deployment ID
   - verify /health
   - verify /version
   - verify production SHA
6. Disable only the affected feature when feature flags permit.
7. Keep unaffected parts of IVX online.
8. Notify the owner only for:
   - production outage
   - security issue
   - data-loss risk
   - failed rollback
   - approval required

Target:

- detection: under 30 seconds where monitoring supports it
- initial containment: under 5 minutes
- automatic rollback: under 10 minutes where safe

Do not fabricate timing results.

Measure and report actual times.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — AUTOMATIC ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS
==================================================

For every incident:

1. Read complete logs.
2. Correlate client, backend, database and deployment traces.
3. Compare failing SHA with last known healthy SHA.
4. Identify the first relevant code/configuration change.
5. Reproduce the failure in an isolated environment.
6. Classify the root cause:
   - source code
   - configuration
   - credential
   - infrastructure
   - dependency
   - database
   - network
   - timeout
   - concurrency
   - data corruption
   - mobile platform
7. Return:
   - exact file
   - exact function
   - exact line when available
   - root cause
   - reproduction steps
   - confidence
   - risk level
   - proposed repair
   - rollback option

Do not call the incident fixed until it was reproduced before the repair and passes afterward.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — SAFE SELF-REPAIR
==================================================

For each safe repair:

1. Create:
   auto-fix/<incident-id>

2. Add a regression test reproducing the failure.

3. Confirm the test fails before the fix.

4. Apply the smallest safe repair.

5. Run:
   - focused tests
   - TypeScript
   - lint
   - unit tests
   - integration tests
   - affected E2E tests
   - secret scan
   - dependency audit

6. Review the diff.

7. Commit.

8. Push.

9. Open a PR.

10. Monitor CI.

11. Repair CI failures related to the change.

Never edit main directly.

Never combine unrelated incidents in one PR.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — AUTONOMOUS REPAIR PERMISSIONS
==================================================

Autonomous may repair without owner approval:

- TypeScript failures
- lint failures
- broken imports
- malformed workflow YAML
- test fixtures
- bounded timeout logic
- safe retry logic
- loading states
- cache defects
- duplicate requests
- duplicate chat subscriptions
- non-destructive UI defects
- safe performance improvements
- dead-code removal
- documentation
- test coverage

Owner approval required for:

- production deployment
- database migrations
- RLS changes
- authentication behavior
- payment logic
- deleting data
- secrets or credential rotation
- Android/iOS production signing
- AWS, DNS, Render or Supabase configuration
- destructive refactors
- large architectural changes

==================================================
PHASE 7 — DEPLOYMENT AND VERIFICATION GATE
==================================================

A repair may be marked VERIFIED only after:

- PR approved and merged
- GitHub main SHA captured
- CI tested SHA captured
- Render deployment ID captured
- Render status LIVE
- /health HTTP 200
- /version HTTP 200
- smoke tests pass
- affected incident no longer reproduces
- no regression increase
- rollback remains available

Required equality:

GitHub main SHA
=
CI tested SHA
=
Render deployed SHA
=
/health SHA
=
/version SHA

If any value differs:

- status = FAILED_VERIFICATION
- rollback automatically when safe
- never mark COMPLETED

==================================================
PHASE 8 — CRASH RECOVERY FOR IVX IA AND WORKERS
==================================================

Verify recovery after:

- Render restart
- autonomous-worker restart
- mobile-app restart
- network interruption
- GitHub timeout
- Supabase timeout
- deployment interruption
- CI interruption

Required behavior:

- job state persists
- incident state persists
- heartbeat resumes
- no duplicate commit
- no duplicate PR
- no duplicate deployment
- no false completion
- failed ledger result remains authoritative
- execution resumes from the last safe checkpoint

==================================================
PHASE 9 — FULL MODULE STABILITY QA
==================================================

Continuously verify:

- owner login
- logout/login
- password recovery
- session persistence
- member registration
- investor registration
- buyer registration
- properties
- deals
- reels
- chat
- message ordering
- message duplication
- attachments
- media uploads
- notifications
- Admin Hub
- Owner Dashboard
- settings
- autonomous control
- API health
- database health
- Android startup
- iOS startup
- web startup

Test:

- cold start
- warm start
- weak network
- network loss
- restored network
- Render restart
- app restart
- long-running session
- large chat history
- concurrent requests
- repeated login
- repeated upload

==================================================
PHASE 10 — CONTROLLED SELF-HEALING CERTIFICATION
==================================================

Run these controlled tests safely:

TEST 1:
Controlled TypeScript fixture failure.

TEST 2:
Controlled API timeout fixture.

TEST 3:
Controlled duplicate-chat-message fixture.

TEST 4:
Controlled failed deployment verification.

TEST 5:
Controlled worker restart during execution.

For each test, Autonomous must:

- detect
- create incident
- reproduce
- create branch
- add regression test
- repair
- pass tests
- commit
- push
- open PR
- pass CI
- request approval where required
- deploy
- verify
- close incident
- return evidence

Required evidence:

- incident ID
- job ID
- trace ID
- branch
- commit SHA
- PR URL
- CI run ID
- deployment ID
- runtime SHA
- detection time
- containment time
- repair time
- rollback result
- final status

==================================================
PHASE 11 — 24/7 AUTONOMOUS OPERATION
==================================================

Maintain a prioritized queue:

P0:
- outage
- security
- data integrity
- authentication
- failed deployment
- critical mobile crash

P1:
- CI
- chat stability
- registration
- uploads
- notifications
- performance

P2:
- architecture
- cleanup
- coverage
- documentation
- technical debt

Autonomous must always select the highest-priority safe task.

Routine engineering must continue without repeated owner prompts.

==================================================
PHASE 12 — REPORTING
==================================================

Post concise reports in IVX IA Chat:

Every two hours:

- incidents detected
- incidents contained
- incidents repaired
- crashes by platform
- active task
- completed tasks
- PRs
- CI status
- deployment status
- GitHub SHA
- Render SHA
- runtime SHA
- rollbacks
- owner approvals required
- next three priorities

Executive reports:

- 7:00 AM
- 7:00 PM

Do not post duplicate narrative reports.

==================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE
==================================================

Return:

SELF_HEALING_ACTIVE_VERIFIED

only when:

- continuous scan is active
- real-time crash monitoring is active
- incidents persist durably
- containment works
- rollback works
- auto-fix branches work
- regression tests are mandatory
- deployment verification works
- SHA parity is enforced
- restart recovery works
- five controlled incidents pass
- no job is falsely marked completed
- required CI workflows pass
- Android/iOS crash evidence is available
- owner controls production and credentials

Otherwise return:

SELF_HEALING_NOT_VERIFIED

and list only the exact remaining blockers.

START NOW.

First restore GitHub Actions runner execution.
Then establish the clean canonical main checkout.
Then activate the continuous scan.
Then execute the controlled self-healing certification tests.

Do not promise zero crashes.
Prove rapid detection, safe containment, verified repair and automatic rollback.
